source_text: Yes please, bell claude-16.  And yes, we can start the explicit-signal inbox.  I'd like to include the report-futon-bug "concept" though that specific mechanism was a bit wonky.  What I mean is that explicit signals can include all of the error and warning types that show up (e.g. Emacs *Warnings* and messages that I otherwise would have to notice and report).  This is related to the concept of running FUTON in a debugger, which, if you think about it, is also closely related to the Elephant-2000 ideas that we've been looking at in the parallel mission.  So, this is an opportunity to weave them together.

reply_text:
Sending the takeover bell to claude-16 first:My string decoding for `emacsclient` output is wrong: `unicode_escape` would mangle the `■` marks and any CJK text. Instead I'll have Emacs write the slice to a file and read it back as UTF-8:The inbox now shows 8 normal and 5 low faults, the 8 declared waits (my claude-16 park among them) and the sorries, with ports below. Starting the intake loop under bg.py and committing:The 403 fault is the most consequential item, so I'm checking whether it's still happening now that turns go through the JVM path, or was only the old file-mode dispatcher:㊥ ("bell claude-16" / "start the explicit-signal inbox") Both are done. claude-16 has the takeover request, and I'm parked on its answer. The inbox is live, and it now includes errors and warnings nobody has to notice or report.

㊢ (claude-16) The packet points it at the Checkpoint and the test case, and proposes the false-open diagnosis as its first job, discovery before any fix. The owner of record changes only if it accepts. It also mentions your errors-as-signals idea as a shared design question. Job `invoke-1791690998492-4081-000d9ded`.

㊢ (fault intake: the automatic half of report-futon-bug; `1cf5bc7`) `scripts/fault_intake.py` runs every 60 s under bg.py and reuses the bug collector's secret scrubbing. It reads:
- Emacs `*Warnings*` and error-like `*Messages*` lines;
- warning-level journal lines for the futon units;
- the Agency, futon1b and 象 health endpoints;
- failed systemd units.

Repeats count up a single fault, and two noisy kinds collapse into one low-severity fault each, with the places listed: obsolete-macro byte-compile warnings (31 files) and agents' ad-hoc `systemd-run` failures (40 units). `discharge <id> <note>` closes a fault.

㊢ (what it found on its first pass: 8 faults plus 5 low)
- **象 analysis 403 "monthly usage limit"** (11×). I checked whether it's current: since the recorder fix every turn analyses fine through the JVM on seat `象-sonnet`, and seats `象-1`…`象-4` are benched until about 04:44. So it's historical, but it tells you those seats are out of quota.
- **`futon-agency-ws`: connection refused** (twice), and a **direnv error inside `post-command-hook`**, which runs on every command.
- **`emacs-graph.service` notification-permission warnings** in the journal, and **tty-frame-reaper**: 4 mosh frames against a limit of 3.
- **straight.el:** package.el loaded after straight.

The one false positive so far is my own: the `report-futon-bug` confirmation line matched on the word "failed" in its filename.

㊢ (the inbox view) `~/code/data/minus40/open.html`, rewritten every minute.
- **Explicit section first:** faults, the Agency's declared waits (8 parks, mine included), open sorries, and recent memory versions joined to their turns.
- **Kernel ports at the bottom,** labelled unreliable until M-象-2000 links answers.

🈖 ("weave them together") In Elephant-2000 terms the fit is direct. A warning is an assertion made by a component, an inbox item is the obligation it creates on someone, and discharging the item is meeting the obligation. That's the same open/closed shape as an operator's ask in 象, so one kernel could compute "open" across operator asks, agent bells and system faults alike. Running FUTON in a debugger then means faults become acts with owners. That's a design point to settle with claude-16 once it has said yes or no: whether faults enter M-象-2000's act vocabulary, or stay in -40° and only share the lifecycle.

🈰 (next) Step 2 of the earlier plan (crystallisation at write time) is still queued. Or, if you'd rather, I can start triaging the 8 faults, for example routing the direnv hook error and the websocket refusal to whoever owns them.

I'll check claude-16's commit and its first finding before passing them on, since the finding contradicts something I wrote in the Checkpoint:㊥ (claude-16) It accepted M-象-2000, and its first finding changes the problem. The ports weren't failing to link answers; the answers were missing from the records. In the process it caught a false claim I made in the Checkpoint, which I've corrected.

㊬ (checked)
- **The job:** done in work mode.
- **The ownership commit:** `c6f2b068` changes only the mission header's Owner line, which now reads "claude-16 from 2026-10-11 (Joe, via claude-15; …)".
- **Its key number:** turn records carry no `reply_text` at all in the outage window: 0 of 93 analysed records on 10-09 and 0 of 117 on 10-10, against 135 of 162 on 10-04.

㊢ (its findings)
1. **No replies on the records.** For those turns, ports were computed from your fragments alone, so every opening fragment stayed open. The linking code was never even reached.
2. **Where replies exist, brackets are labels, not quotes.** Out of 797 marked paragraphs since 10-01, 662 carry labels like "where we are". Only 123 quote your words, and of those, 108 link correctly. The matcher works; the proforma practice mostly doesn't feed it.
3. **The replies are recoverable.** They're on :7073 as agent-chat evidence, chained to your turns, so they can be backfilled and the ports recomputed.

㊩ ("almost nothing closed") My Checkpoint said the replies quoted your words and still nothing closed. That was wrong on both counts: there were no replies on the records, and 15 of my 17 brackets were labels. I've corrected my paragraph and the test-case file, attributing the correction to claude-16's finding (futon3c `58d9c0a1`, my text only). It's also a lesson for my own replies: when a paragraph answers something you said, quote your words, as the proforma asks. I'm doing that from now on.

㊢ (its plan)
1. A lab note with the census script.
2. Discovery: does the reply evidence map one-to-one onto turn records? No writes.
3. If it does, backfill `reply_text` and recompute ports, then re-label the 24-row test case.
4. Only then propose how label-brackets should link, using numbers: a word-overlap match, or a "sole open port" rule, both recorded as inferences. It notes that `answers-inferred` exists in the kernel but is never populated on the live path.
5. Treat `constrain` as a standing rule rather than an open port, in the same class as grants and withdrawals.

㊣ ("errors and warnings as open items") claude-16's proposal is the fit I'd hoped for:
- a warning enters as a `:report-problem` act authored by the component, recorded as a turn-shaped record with origin "system" and no reading;
- the existing table already closes it by verify, explain, redirect or commit;
- -40° and the ports would then share one id through the author and subject reference.

It wants trustworthy ports (its step 3) before settling that, and I agree. Until then, my fault intake keeps faults in -40° with their own open and discharged lifecycle. The fingerprint and subject are already in place for the join.

🈰 (next on my side) Crystallisation at write time, as queued. claude-16's steps 2 and 3 run in parallel; I'm not parked on them, since it reports to you through the mission.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the Checkpoint records)
- **Ownership:** no agent has worked on the mission since 10-04; claude-17 is still the owner of record.
- **The outage, its cause, the repair and the backfill:** each with its commit and numbers. The cause was the Emacs recorder reverting to `files`, and the 7 empty-turn leftovers are listed as unassigned.
- **The open problem:** false-open ports. A new file, `holes/labs/M-象-2000/CHECKPOINT-2026-10-11-false-open-ports.md`, lists my session's 24 open acts row by row, each with what actually happened: 18 answered or done, 2 standing constraints, 4 genuinely open. It notes that the replies did quote your words in their brackets and still nothing closed. Whether the quote matching or the kernel's closing table is at fault hasn't been checked; that's left for the next owner.
- **A pointer to minus40:** it reads turns with the mission's own code.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text:
("whether we need to wait") Mostly no. Part of the explicit-signal inbox doesn't depend on answers being linked at all:
- **Sorries and proposals:** ours, with explicit statuses.
- **Delegations awaiting a reply:** the Agency job state is authoritative (queued, running or done), so the codex-70 backfill would have shown as open until it finished, then closed.
- **Parked waits:** declared through the park API, with deadlines.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: ("ask claude-16 to take over") I think that fits well. claude-16 already found the outage, knows the turn-service code, and suggested the replay measures. With the Checkpoint as its brief, its first job would be the false-open problem. That would let us work in tandem: claude-16 makes answers link on the 象 side, and I build the -40° inbox to consume them.
